body.statement: Does \(q(v)>0\) for every \(v\in\Omega_V\), together with the calibrated restrictions \(\rho\ge\delta\) and \(d_M\ge\delta\), imply both that every moment vector of an arbitrary admissible SCM has an equal-moment representative in the bounded finite legal fiber and that every limiting vector of bounded graph-legal moments has an equal-moment finite SCM whose actual selected MAG remains in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\)? Resolve first the binary three-observed-variable COPAG with a compelled collider by stratifying the invariant essential-feature polynomials \(Z_e\). An affirmative resolution must give a legal lift for every boundary stratum; a negative resolution must give a positive rational \(q\), a rational \(\delta\), and an algebraic endpoint for which the negative certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) excludes every legal architecture.
body.justification: This remains the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact actual-parent graph semantics and attained extrema for the full arbitrary-SCM class.
body.gap: Openness and density of faithful laws do not supply an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary or an unattained causal endpoint.
body.consumer: Its resolution determines whether exact-graph COPAG bounds beyond the bounded compiler and saturated subclass may be reported as attained without extra graph-strength assumptions.

obligation.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
obligation.obstruction: The selected-cell and intervention moments are linear in each source law separately, but \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in its own source law.  An \(m+3\)-point barycentric reduction can therefore send a positive essentiality witness to zero.  Exact barycenter preservation with prescribed positive witness atoms can fail on a proper face, and the frozen assumptions impose neither faithfulness nor minimum feature strength.  Exogenizing hidden endogenous variables must also preserve actual functional dependencies, not only a permitted latent projection.
obligation.attempted: Directed-feature indicators can be appended to the sourcewise moment vector because they are separately linear, but the two-copy source-feature polynomial remains nonlinear in the compressed source.  Retaining an explicit witness pair does not guarantee exact barycenter preservation with positive weights.  The positive exclusive-or support-deletion family demonstrates failure of the naive route, although its illegal boundary has an equal-moment legal lift and is not a negative certificate.  The compelled-collider case closes only for an isolated selection root, as recorded in the partial result.
obligation.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\), let \(S\) be an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) of Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): start with intervals of the prescribed lengths and, whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Since \(0<p_{xy}<1\), each exchange is possible; finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), recursive truncated factorization gives the single selected-intervention value
\[
\theta=
\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
\bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction.  Hence the exact-graph value and every response-support boundary representation of it have a legal lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, and it does not preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.
